# Overview

This document fits statistical distributions to the pooled extractables concentration data reported by Nahan et al. (2020). The goal is to characterise the empirical concentration distribution of extractables from additive-manufactured ABS medical devices, for use in quantification-bias simulations.

**Reference:** Nahan K., Sussman E.M., Oktem B., Schultheis L., Wickramasekara S. (2020). *Screening for extractables in additive-manufactured acrylonitrile butadiene styrene orthopedic cast.* Talanta, 212, 120464. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.talanta.2019.120464>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1 · Raw data from Nahan et al.

Data are taken from the supplementary information of Nahan et al. (2020), which extends Tables 1–2 of the main article. Units are **µg g⁻¹** (micrograms per gram of extracted material). Non-detected observations are coded as `"N.D."`.

Five material types were studied:

| Code    | Description                                              |
|---------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| USPF    | USP Class VI medical-grade ABS filament                  |
| C-USPF  | Cast (finished device) manufactured from USPF            |
| CGF     | Consumer-grade ABS filament                              |
| UFC-CGF | **Un**finished cast manufactured from CGF                |
| FC-CGF  | **F**inished (post-processed) cast manufactured from CGF |

Two analytical methods were used:

- **GC/MS** — (Table 1 of the paper)
- **LC/MS (positive ion mode only)** — (Table 2 of the paper)

> **Note — exclusion of negative-ion LC/MS data (Table 3):** Table 3 of Nahan et al. reports only 7 quantified observations across all five materials and three solvents (compared to ≈ 100 observations in the positive-ion dataset), which is insufficient to fit a separate distribution.
>
> **Assumption:** The log-normal fit derived from positive-ion LC/MS data (Table 2) is used as the representative LC/MS concentration distribution for all simulation scenarios.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(fitdistrplus)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(scales)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2 · Unit conversion and LOQ censoring

Reported concentrations (µg g⁻¹ material) are converted to µg mL⁻¹ in the undiluted extract by applying the extraction ratio used in the study:

$$C_{\text{extract}} \;[\mu\text{g mL}^{-1}] \;=\;
  C_{\text{material}} \;[\mu\text{g g}^{-1}] \;\times\; 0.2 \;[\text{g mL}^{-1}]$$

where 0.2 g mL⁻¹ is the extraction ratio used by Nahan et al. (0.2 g material per 1 mL solvent; ISO 10993-12, 50 °C, 24 h).

Limits of quantification (LOQ) stated in the paper (Sections 2.3 and 2.4):

| Method | LOQ (instrument) | LOQ (material) | LOQ (extract, used here) |
|--------|------------------|----------------|--------------------------|
| GC/MS  | 100 µg L⁻¹       | 1.0 µg g⁻¹     | **0.2 µg mL⁻¹**          |
| LC/MS  | 500 µg L⁻¹       | 2.5 µg g⁻¹     | **0.5 µg mL⁻¹**          |

The LOQ in extract units is obtained as: LOQ_material × 0.2 g mL⁻¹.

```{r loq}
# Limits of quantification in µg mL⁻¹ (extract units after ×0.2 conversion).
# GC/MS: 1.0 µg g⁻¹ × 0.2 g mL⁻¹ = 0.2 µg mL⁻¹  (Nahan et al., Section 2.3)
# LC/MS: 2.5 µg g⁻¹ × 0.2 g mL⁻¹ = 0.5 µg mL⁻¹  (Nahan et al., Section 2.4)
loq_gc <- 0.2   # µg mL⁻¹
loq_lc <- 0.5   # µg mL⁻¹

# Convert from µg g⁻¹ to µg mL⁻¹ (extraction ratio = 0.2 g mL⁻¹).
# suppressWarnings() silences coercion of "N.D." strings to NA.
gc_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(all_gcms_raw) * 0.2)
lc_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(all_lcms_raw) * 0.2)

# ── Build left/right interval matrix required by fitdistcens ─────────────────
# Convention (Turnbull, 1976; fitdistrplus documentation):
#   • Detected observation  : left = right = measured value  (exact)
#   • Non-detected (< LOQ)  : left = NA,  right = LOQ        (left-censored)
gc_cens <- data.frame(
  left  = ifelse(is.na(gc_num), NA,      gc_num),
  right = ifelse(is.na(gc_num), loq_gc,  gc_num)
)

lc_cens <- data.frame(
  left  = ifelse(is.na(lc_num), NA,      lc_num),
  right = ifelse(is.na(lc_num), loq_lc,  lc_num)
)

# ── Proportion below LOQ (censoring fraction) ────────────────────────────────
gcms_nd_pct <- sum(is.na(gc_num)) / length(gc_num) * 100
lcms_nd_pct <- sum(is.na(lc_num)) / length(lc_num) * 100

cat(sprintf("Pooled GC/MS  — n total: %d | N.D.: %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            length(gc_num), sum(is.na(gc_num)), gcms_nd_pct))
cat(sprintf("Pooled LC/MS  — n total: %d | N.D.: %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            length(lc_num), sum(is.na(lc_num)), lcms_nd_pct))
cat(sprintf("\nGC/MS detected range: %.2f – %.1f µg mL⁻¹\n",
            min(gc_num, na.rm = TRUE), max(gc_num, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("LC/MS detected range: %.2f – %.1f µg mL⁻¹\n",
            min(lc_num, na.rm = TRUE), max(lc_num, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3 · Distribution fitting (censored MLE)

Normal, log-normal, and gamma distributions are fitted by maximum likelihood using in `fitdistrplus::fitdistcens()` (Delignette-Muller & Dutang, 2015). AIC is used for model comparison.

```{r fit}
# ── GC/MS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fit_gc_norm  <- fitdistcens(gc_cens, "norm")
fit_gc_lnorm <- fitdistcens(gc_cens, "lnorm")
fit_gc_gamma <- fitdistcens(gc_cens, "gamma")

# ── LC/MS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fit_lc_norm  <- fitdistcens(lc_cens, "norm")
fit_lc_lnorm <- fitdistcens(lc_cens, "lnorm")
fit_lc_gamma <- fitdistcens(lc_cens, "gamma")

# ── AIC comparison ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("GC/MS AIC:\n")
print(c(
  Normal    = round(summary(fit_gc_norm)$aic,  2),
  LogNormal = round(summary(fit_gc_lnorm)$aic, 2),
  Gamma     = round(summary(fit_gc_gamma)$aic, 2)
))

cat("\nLC/MS AIC:\n")
print(c(
  Normal    = round(summary(fit_lc_norm)$aic,  2),
  LogNormal = round(summary(fit_lc_lnorm)$aic, 2),
  Gamma     = round(summary(fit_lc_gamma)$aic, 2)
))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4 · Log-normal parameter estimates

Log-normal distributions are expected for extractables concentration data.

```{r lnorm-summary}
cat("── GC/MS log-normal fit ─────────────────────────────────────\n")
summary(fit_gc_lnorm)

cat("\n── LC/MS log-normal fit ─────────────────────────────────────\n")
summary(fit_lc_lnorm)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5 · Q–Q plots

Q–Q plots assess goodness of fit for each candidate distribution. Only detected values are plotted (censored observations are excluded from the empirical quantiles).

```{r qqplots, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
df_gc <- data.frame(conc = na.omit(gc_num))
df_lc <- data.frame(conc = na.omit(lc_num))

# ── GC/MS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
q_gc_n <- ggplot(df_gc, aes(sample = conc)) +
  stat_qq(distribution = qnorm,
          dparams = list(mean = fit_gc_norm$estimate["mean"],
                         sd   = fit_gc_norm$estimate["sd"]),
          alpha = 0.5) +
  stat_qq_line(distribution = qnorm,
               dparams = list(mean = fit_gc_norm$estimate["mean"],
                              sd   = fit_gc_norm$estimate["sd"]),
               color = "darkblue") +
  labs(title = "Pooled GC/MS: Normal",
       x = "Theoretical quantiles (µg mL⁻¹)",
       y = "Sample quantiles (µg mL⁻¹)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

q_gc_ln <- ggplot(df_gc, aes(sample = log(conc))) +
  stat_qq(distribution = qnorm,
          dparams = list(mean = fit_gc_lnorm$estimate["meanlog"],
                         sd   = fit_gc_lnorm$estimate["sdlog"]),
          alpha = 0.5) +
  stat_qq_line(distribution = qnorm,
               dparams = list(mean = fit_gc_lnorm$estimate["meanlog"],
                              sd   = fit_gc_lnorm$estimate["sdlog"]),
               color = "darkred") +
  labs(title = "Pooled GC/MS: Log-normal",
       x = "Theoretical normal quantiles (log µg mL⁻¹)",
       y = "Sample quantiles (log µg mL⁻¹)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

q_gc_g <- ggplot(df_gc, aes(sample = conc)) +
  stat_qq(distribution = qgamma,
          dparams = list(shape = fit_gc_gamma$estimate["shape"],
                         rate  = fit_gc_gamma$estimate["rate"]),
          alpha = 0.5) +
  stat_qq_line(distribution = qgamma,
               dparams = list(shape = fit_gc_gamma$estimate["shape"],
                              rate  = fit_gc_gamma$estimate["rate"]),
               color = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "Pooled GC/MS: Gamma",
       x = "Theoretical quantiles (µg mL⁻¹)",
       y = "Sample quantiles (µg mL⁻¹)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

q_gc_n + q_gc_ln + q_gc_g

# ── LC/MS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
q_lc_n <- ggplot(df_lc, aes(sample = conc)) +
  stat_qq(distribution = qnorm,
          dparams = list(mean = fit_lc_norm$estimate["mean"],
                         sd   = fit_lc_norm$estimate["sd"]),
          alpha = 0.5) +
  stat_qq_line(distribution = qnorm,
               dparams = list(mean = fit_lc_norm$estimate["mean"],
                              sd   = fit_lc_norm$estimate["sd"]),
               color = "darkblue") +
  labs(title = "Pooled LC/MS: Normal",
       x = "Theoretical quantiles (µg mL⁻¹)",
       y = "Sample quantiles (µg mL⁻¹)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

q_lc_ln <- ggplot(df_lc, aes(sample = log(conc))) +
  stat_qq(distribution = qnorm,
          dparams = list(mean = fit_lc_lnorm$estimate["meanlog"],
                         sd   = fit_lc_lnorm$estimate["sdlog"]),
          alpha = 0.5) +
  stat_qq_line(distribution = qnorm,
               dparams = list(mean = fit_lc_lnorm$estimate["meanlog"],
                              sd   = fit_lc_lnorm$estimate["sdlog"]),
               color = "darkred") +
  labs(title = "Pooled LC/MS: Log-normal",
       x = "Theoretical normal quantiles (log µg mL⁻¹)",
       y = "Sample quantiles (log µg mL⁻¹)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

q_lc_g <- ggplot(df_lc, aes(sample = conc)) +
  stat_qq(distribution = qgamma,
          dparams = list(shape = fit_lc_gamma$estimate["shape"],
                         rate  = fit_lc_gamma$estimate["rate"]),
          alpha = 0.5) +
  stat_qq_line(distribution = qgamma,
               dparams = list(shape = fit_lc_gamma$estimate["shape"],
                              rate  = fit_lc_gamma$estimate["rate"]),
               color = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "Pooled LC/MS: Gamma",
       x = "Theoretical quantiles (µg mL⁻¹)",
       y = "Sample quantiles (µg mL⁻¹)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

q_lc_n + q_lc_ln + q_lc_g
```

# 6 · Simulated concentration distributions at varying AET thresholds

This section simulates concentration distributions under five scenarios and plots them against analytical evaluation thresholds (AETs) of 0.45, 3, 6, and 36 µg mL⁻¹ — spanning typical AET ranges discussed in ISO 10993-18 and the extractables/leachables literature.

The five scenarios are:

1.  **Uniform (0.4 – 1.4 × AET):** concentration clustered tightly around the AET
2.  **Uniform (0.3 – 1.3 × AET):** slightly wider uniform, slightly shifted
3.  **GC/MS log-normal:** parametrised from the Nahan et al. pooled GC/MS fit
4.  **LC/MS log-normal:** parametrised from the Nahan et al. pooled LC/MS fit
5.  **Custom scaled:** from Rozio et al.

```{r aet-plots, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
set.seed(42)
N_extractables <- 800000   # number of simulated extractables per scenario

# ── Base distributions (fixed across AET levels) ─────────────────────────────
# Parameters taken from the censored MLE fits above (Section 4).
base_lognorm_gcms <- rlnorm(N_extractables,
                             meanlog = fit_gc_lnorm$estimate["meanlog"],
                             sdlog   = fit_gc_lnorm$estimate["sdlog"])

base_lognorm_lcms <- rlnorm(N_extractables,
                             meanlog = fit_lc_lnorm$estimate["meanlog"],
                             sdlog   = fit_lc_lnorm$estimate["sdlog"])

# Custom scenario
# (70 % of extractables at low concentration, 20 % mid, 10 % high)
S  <- runif(N_extractables, min = 0, max = 1)^2
p1 <- round(0.70 * N_extractables)
p2 <- round(0.90 * N_extractables)
custom_scaled <- sample(c(
  S[1:p1],
  S[(p1 + 1):p2] * 10,
  S[(p2 + 1):N_extractables] * 100
))

# ── AET scenarios ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
aet_scenarios <- c(0.45, 3, 6, 36)

for (aet in aet_scenarios) {

  uniform_1 <- runif(N_extractables, min = 0.4 * aet, max = 1.4 * aet)
  uniform_2 <- runif(N_extractables, min = 0.3 * aet, max = 1.3 * aet)

  scenario_data <- tibble(
    `1. Uniform (0.4 to 1.4 × AET)` = uniform_1,
    `2. Uniform (0.3 to 1.3 × AET)` = uniform_2,
    `3. GC/MS log-normal (Nahan et al.)`    = base_lognorm_gcms,
    `4. LC/MS log-normal (Nahan et al.)`    = base_lognorm_lcms,
    `5. Custom (Rozio et al.)`     = custom_scaled
  ) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = everything(),
      names_to  = "Distribution_Type",
      values_to = "Concentration"
    )

  p <- ggplot(scenario_data, aes(x = Concentration)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(fill = Distribution_Type),
                   position = "identity", bins = 100,
                   color = "black", alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = aet,
               color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    annotate("text", x = aet * 1.05, y = Inf, vjust = 1.5, hjust = 0,
             label = paste("AET =", aet, "µg mL⁻¹"),
             color = "red", size = 3.5) +
    scale_x_log10(
      breaks = trans_breaks("log10", function(x) 10^x),
      labels = trans_format("log10", math_format(10^.x))
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      name   = "Distribution scenario",
      values = c(
        "1. Uniform (0.4 to 1.4 × AET)" = "mediumpurple",
        "2. Uniform (0.3 to 1.3 × AET)" = "orchid",
        "3. GC/MS log-normal (Nahan et al.)"    = "darkorange",
        "4. LC/MS log-normal (Nahan et al.)"    = "dodgerblue",
        "5. Custom (Rozio et al.)"     = "seagreen"
      )
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      legend.position  = "top",
      legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold")
    ) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Concentration distributions vs. AET =", aet, "µg mL⁻¹"),
      x     = "Concentration (log₁₀ scale, µg mL⁻¹)",
      y     = "Frequency"
    )

  print(p)
}
```
